overview: This Senate resolution honors the life of Reverend Jesse Louis Jackson, Sr., a civil rights leader who died on February 17, 2026. It traces his work alongside Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., his founding of Operation PUSH, a group focused on economic opportunity for Black Americans, and of the National Rainbow Coalition, his presidential campaigns in 1984 and 1988, his role in freeing a captured U.S. Navy pilot in Syria in 1983, and his service as a special envoy to Africa. The Senate commends his contributions, offers condolences to his family, and asks that a copy be sent to them. It was approved on March 16, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution rightly honors a major figure of the civil rights movement whose decades of advocacy shaped American public life.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
